Why This Is Asked
- Tests cross-cluster policy propagation, conflict handling, and secure identity management
- Validates runtime enforcement by per-tenant sidecars in a multi-cluster CNF gateway mesh

Key Concepts
- CustomResourceDefinition for TenantPolicy
- Cross-cluster replication with mTLS and SPIFFE IDs
- Dynamic gateway policy loading in sidecars
- Conflict resolution and eventual consistency

Code Example
```yaml
# CRD: TenantPolicy
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantpolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenantID:
                type: string
              namespaces:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: string
              rules:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    action:
                      type: string
                      enum: [allow, deny]
                    resources:
                      type: array
                      items:
                        type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: tenantpolicies
    singular: tenantpolicy
    kind: TenantPolicy
```

```yaml
# Policy Agent Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: policy-agent
  namespace: cnf-system
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: policy-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: policy-agent
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: agent
        image: policy-agent:latest
        env:
        - name: REMOTE_CLUSTER
          value: "peer-cluster.example.com"
        - name: SPIFFE_TRUST_DOMAIN
          value: "example.com"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: spiffe-bundle
          mountPath: /run/spiffe
      volumes:
      - name: spiffe-bundle
        configMap:
          name: spiffe-bundle
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical design of per-tenant isolation and backpressure in a CNF proxy, using Redis for atomic bulkhead checks and a sidecar pattern that’s common in Kubernetes CNF deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Bulkhead per tenant
- Redis atomic operations via Lua scripting
- Backpressure with 429 and simple per-tenant queue
- Sidecar wiring in a multi-tenant CNF

## Code Example
```lua
-- Atomic bulkhead check
local slots = KEYS[1]
local queue = KEYS[2]
local limit = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local payload = ARGV[2]

local current = tonumber(redis.call('GET', slots) or '0')
if current < limit then
  redis.call('INCR', slots)
  redis.call('EXPIRE', slots, 60)
  return { 'acquired' }
else
  local qlen = tonumber(redis.call('LLEN', queue) or '0')
  if qlen < 10 then
    redis.call('LPUSH', queue, payload)
    return { 'queued' }
  else
    return { 'full' }
  end
end
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test under burst traffic and verify queue draining?
- What happens on sidecar restart and how do you prevent slot leakage?
- What are trade-offs of Redis-backed queues vs in-memory buffers?

```go
func shouldSample(tenantID, traceID string, rate float64) bool {

    return float64(sampled) < rate*10000
}
```

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfnamespacesecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
        listKind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraintList
        plural: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraints
        singular: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraint
  targets:
  - target: admissionreviews
    rego: |
      package cnfnamespacesecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.hostNetwork
        msg := "hostNetwork is forbidden for CNFs"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers
        # fallback for non-pods
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
        msg := "readOnlyRootFilesystem is required for all containers"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.privileged == true
        msg := "privileged containers are disallowed"
      }
```

```yaml
spec:
```

## Code Example

```yaml
  - path: /api/v1/users/*

  - path: /health
```

## Implementation Details

### ConfigMap Structure
The sidecar watches ConfigMaps matching the pattern `cnf.acl.{tenant}.yaml` in the tenant's namespace. Namespace-scoped overrides follow the naming convention `cnf.acl.{tenant}.override.yaml`.

### Watch Mechanism
Use a Kubernetes Informer to watch ConfigMap changes. On update, the sidecar re-parses the YAML, merges policies (namespace overrides take precedence), and updates the in-memory rule engine without pod restart.

### Conflict Resolution
When cluster-wide and namespace-scoped policies conflict, apply a merge strategy where namespace-specific rules override cluster defaults for the same path and method combination. Log conflicts for observability.

```yaml
      - path: /api/v1/users/*

      - path: /health

```

## Code Example
```yaml
# Tenant CRD (simplified)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenants.cnf.example.com
spec:
  group: cnf.example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenantID: { type: string }
              namespace: { type: string }
              desiredVersion: { type: string }
  scope: Cluster
  names:
    plural: tenants
    singular: tenant
    kind: Tenant
    shortNames: [ tns ]
```

```yaml
# Tenant canary Deployment (tenant-a)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        tenant: tenant-a
        version: v2
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: registry.example/cnf/gateway:v2
```

```yaml
# Istio TrafficSplit example for canary (tenant-a)
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  http:
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local
        subset: v1
      weight: 90
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local
        subset: v2
      weight: 10
```
